articles.title_zh: 'Can you believe it?': SpaceX catches part of its Starship rocket on return to Earth
facts_zh:
'Can you believe it?': SpaceX catches part of its Starship rocket on return to Earth
SpaceX has successfully caught the top part of its huge Starship rocket on its return to Earth for the first time.
"Can you believe it?," a commentator said as large crowds cheered at the launch site in Texas.
The company had hoped to catch both the bottom and upper stages of the rocket using mechanical arms - nicknamed chopsticks - on its launch tower.

articles.title_original: 'Miracle on Mississippi' - All passengers rescued after New Orleans cruise ship collision
articles.title_zh: 'Miracle on Mississippi' - All passengers rescued after New Orleans cruise ship collision
facts_zh:
'Miracle on Mississippi' - All passengers rescued after New Orleans cruise ship collision
- Published
Some 130 people on a cruise ship docked in New Orleans have been rescued after it was struck by a tanker.
The cruise ship, American Heritage, was left lying on its side in the Mississippi River after it was hit by the cargo vessel Atlantic Asphalt.
The collision left 32 people from the stricken riverboat in hospital with non-critical injuries, but no-one unaccounted for.

all_titles.en: 'Miracle on Mississippi' - All passengers rescued after New Orleans cruise ship collision

articles.title_original: Watch: Cruise ship overturns after collision with tanker in New Orleans
articles.title_zh: Watch: Cruise ship overturns after collision with tanker in New Orleans
facts_zh:
Watch: Cruise ship overturns after collision with tanker in New Orleans
About 130 people were rescued from a cruise ship after it was struck by a tanker while docked in New Orleans, Louisiana on Friday.
Footage shows the American Heritage taking on water following the collision, which left 32 people in hospital with non-critical injuries.
"We have zero people unaccounted for, which truly is a miracle on the Mississippi," New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno told reporters during a press conference.

all_titles.en: Watch: Cruise ship overturns after collision with tanker in New Orleans

articles.title_original: Copper wire upgrade caused nationwide flight suspension, US transport secretary says
articles.title_zh: Copper wire upgrade caused nationwide flight suspension, US transport secretary says
facts_zh:
Copper wire upgrade caused nationwide flight suspension, US transport secretary says
- Published
A nationwide US ground stop that caused thousands of flight cancellations was caused by an issue following a copper wire upgrade, Transport Secretary Sean Duffy said.
Duffy told a news conference that the government was trying to find out whether the problem was caused by "incompetence" on the part of the company doing the upgrades, or faulty equipment.
The US government does not believe it was as a result of a cyber-attack, although an investigation is still under way, Duffy said.

all_titles.en: Copper wire upgrade caused nationwide flight suspension, US transport secretary says

articles.title_original: Italy fines Meta €805m over accessing users' photos
articles.title_zh: Italy fines Meta €805m over accessing users' photos
facts_zh:
Italy fines Meta €805m over accessing users' photos
- Published
Italian regulators have fined social media giant Meta €805m (£670m; $887m) for accessing Android users' photos without their specific consent.
Italy's Data Protection Authority said Meta did not properly inform about 20 million smartphone users that it had access to their photos and videos via a feature of the Facebook app.
It has given Meta 60 days to disable the feature by default and seek users' consent separately.

all_titles.en: Italy fines Meta €805m over accessing users' photos

articles.title_original: Philippines wins first Eurovision Song Contest Asia
articles.title_zh: Philippines wins first Eurovision Song Contest Asia
facts_zh:
Philippines wins first Eurovision Song Contest Asia
- Published
The Philippines have won the very first Eurovision Song Contest Asia, hosted in Bangkok and with 11 countries vying for the title.
Nineteen-year-old singer Carmelle was always a front runner with her women's empowerment anthem Sobra-Sobra, complete with its catchy rap section.
She earned 211 points in total - 93 from the jury and 118 from the public vote - ahead of Thailand's MANG x DAOU in second place with 170 points.

all_titles.en: Philippines wins first Eurovision Song Contest Asia

facts_zh:
Sotheby's auction of $180m Van Gogh challenged over claims it was 'sold under duress'
- Published
Auction house Sotheby's says it is working to resolve a dispute over the intended sale of a painting by Vincent van Gogh.
Châtaigniers en Fleurs, which carries an estimate of $180m (£136m), is due to go under the hammer in New York on Wednesday.
But representatives acting for heirs of the Fischer family - earlier German owners of the work - say it may have been sold under duress during the rise of the Nazis.

articles.title_original: Trump, Putin and Xi plan historic joint meeting in China next week, White House says
articles.title_zh: Trump, Putin and Xi plan historic joint meeting in China next week, White House says
facts_zh:
Trump, Putin and Xi plan historic joint meeting in China next week, White House says
- Published
Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping are planning to meet on the sidelines of a summit in China next week, the White House has said.

The historic meeting between the respective leaders of the US, Russia and China will take place as Trump attends the Asia-Pacific Economic Co-operation (Apec) summit in the southern city of Shenzhen, spokeswoman Olivia Wales told reporters.
"The president has made it clear that, among other topics, he will discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world, whose proliferation President Trump believes is very dangerous," she said.

all_titles.en: Trump, Putin and Xi plan historic joint meeting in China next week, White House says

facts_zh:
What we know about the US ground stop and what to do if your flight is affected
- Published
The US Federal Aviation Administration has lifted the longest nationwide ground stop of flights since the 11 September 2001 attacks.
The FAA said Friday's stoppage, which lasted more than four hours, was "due to extraordinary circumstances" from a communication issue affecting all air traffic control centres.
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there was no indication of a cyber-attack and that everybody was safe.

articles.title_zh: Microsoft says services fully restored after day-long global outage
facts_zh:
Microsoft says services fully restored after day-long global outage
- Published
Microsoft has said its services have been fully restored after a worldwide outage affected several of its tools, causing disruption.
The tech firm said early on Saturday morning that efforts to address the underlying problem had been completed and customers using Outlook, Teams and Copilot should no longer be affected.
The outage hit more than 70 countries, disrupting everything from business operations to government services and personal users.
